rules.title: Auto traits are satisfied structurally
rules.statement: An auto trait (e.g. Send, Sync, Unpin) is satisfied by a concrete type via structural recursion over its composition rather than by an explicit impl, except where an explicit (possibly negative) impl overrides. The error type and the unit/never-shaped Error kind vacuously satisfy every auto trait.

rules.title: Recursive types terminate as satisfied
rules.statement: Auto-trait checking memoizes on key (type, trait); revisiting an in-progress (type, trait) pair during recursion is treated as satisfied (true), so a recursive type does not loop and is not rejected merely for self-reference.

rules.title: Scalars and function pointers satisfy all auto traits
rules.statement: Every scalar type (bool, unit/void, iN/uN incl. i24/u24/i56/u56/i128/u128, f32/f64, integer/float literal types), function items, and function pointers satisfy every auto trait unconditionally.

rules.title: Raw pointers are !Send/!Sync absent an explicit impl
rules.statement: A raw pointer type (*const T / *mut T) does not satisfy a Send/Sync-shaped auto trait unless an explicit positive impl exists for that exact pointer type; a matching explicit impl is honoured (positive accepts, negative rejects).

rules.title: Pointers/references are always Unpin
rules.statement: Raw pointers, &T, and &mut T are Unpin regardless of the pointee's pin-ness, unless an explicit negative Unpin impl exists for that exact pointer type; references never carry a negative Unpin impl and are unconditionally Unpin.

rules.title: &T auto-trait reduces to T: Sync
rules.statement: For a shared reference &T, both Send and Sync are satisfied iff T: Sync. (Send(&T) = Sync(T), Sync(&T) = Sync(T).)

rules.title: &mut T: Send iff T:Send, Sync iff T:Sync
rules.statement: For a mutable reference &mut T, Send(&mut T) = Send(T) and Sync(&mut T) = Sync(T).

rules.title: Type parameter satisfies an auto trait iff bounded by it
rules.statement: A type variable T satisfies auto trait A iff A appears in T's declared bound list in the current generic context; otherwise it does not.

rules.title: Explicit impl overrides structural check for struct/enum
rules.statement: For struct/enum (and zoned struct) types, an explicit auto-trait impl is consulted first by candidate key (mangled concrete name, then full type string, then base name): a positive impl accepts and a negative impl rejects, short-circuiting the structural field/variant walk.

rules.title: Generic positive impl honours its type-param auto-trait bounds
rules.statement: When a positive auto-trait impl has impl type parameters and a generic target, each impl type param is substituted with the corresponding query type argument; for every bound on that param that names an auto trait, the substituted argument must itself satisfy that auto trait, else the impl is rejected.

rules.title: Struct satisfies auto trait iff all fields do
rules.statement: Absent an overriding impl, a struct/zoned-struct satisfies auto trait A iff every field type satisfies A, with generic field TypeVars substituted by the struct's concrete type arguments. An unknown struct (no struct/datatype info) is leniently treated as satisfying.

rules.title: Enum satisfies auto trait iff all variant payloads do
rules.statement: Absent an overriding impl, an enum satisfies auto trait A iff every payload type of every variant satisfies A. An unknown enum is leniently treated as satisfying.

rules.title: UnsafeCell<T> is !Sync; Send follows T
rules.statement: The lang-item logos.lang.cell.UnsafeCell<T> never satisfies Sync; it satisfies Send iff its wrapped T satisfies Send (no arg => not Send). Recognition is by qualified name to avoid clashing with same-named user types.

rules.title: PhantomPinned and #[pinned] types are !Unpin
rules.statement: The lang-item logos.lang.marker.PhantomPinned does not satisfy Unpin; likewise a #[pinned] (arena-resident) struct does not satisfy Unpin. These structural opt-outs propagate via the all-fields rule.

rules.title: Unpin is satisfied by default
rules.statement: Unpin holds for all types except those that (transitively) contain PhantomPinned, are #[pinned], or carry an explicit negative Unpin impl.

rules.title: Array satisfies auto trait iff element does
rules.statement: An array type [T; N] satisfies auto trait A iff its element type T satisfies A; an array with no element type vacuously satisfies.

rules.title: Slice auto-trait reduces to element Sync
rules.statement: A slice type [T] (a shared-reference-shaped view) satisfies Send and Sync iff its element type T satisfies Sync (not the queried trait); an empty-element slice vacuously satisfies.

rules.title: Tuple satisfies auto trait iff all elements do
rules.statement: A tuple type satisfies auto trait A iff every element type satisfies A.

rules.title: Closure auto trait follows its captured types
rules.statement: A closure type satisfies auto trait A iff every captured value's type satisfies A (by-ref captures recorded as &/&mut so reference rules apply). A closure type with no recorded capture set (e.g. a bare dyn Fn annotation without + Send) does not satisfy. Auto-trait satisfaction is computed over captures, not parameter types.

rules.title: Other types conservatively fail auto traits
rules.statement: Any type kind not otherwise handled (e.g. trait objects) is conservatively treated as not satisfying any auto trait.
